Inject structural information from a legal knowledge graph into an open-source LLM as continuous soft tokens during parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and show
measurable improvement over text-only fine-tuning on legal document understanding, under an identical trainable-parameter budget.

Legal NLP already uses citation graphs, but consumes them with encoder-only classifiers. The graph-plus-LLM literature has the fusion techniques, but evaluates on generic benchmarks such as WebQSP and OGB.
Legal graphs add an authority hierarchy, temporal validity windows on provisions, and asymmetric overruling and distinguishing relations that no existing graph-plus-LLM benchmark exercises.
recall at a fixed node budget vs
US or EU source to Indian

Method lineage: LegalBERT / InLegalBERT · SaulLM-7B · LegalBench · LeSICiN heterogeneous statute graphs · LoRA and QLoRA · GraphToken soft-token encoding · G-Retriever PCST subgraph selection · GraphRAG · R-GCN and HGT

Scope note: outputs are document-understanding predictions evaluated retrospectively on benchmarks. The system is not intended to produce legal advice or to inform any decision affecting a real party.
